subject: general
question: The reproductive parts of a flower are:
solution:
The correct answer is __**stamens and pistils**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A flower's **reproductive parts** include the following:

 
 
• **Stamen-**Also known as **Androecium**, this is the **male reproductive organ**. It is made up of two parts: an **anther and filaments**.

 The** anther** is a yellowish sac-like structure that produces and stores pollen.

 The **filament** is a thin, threadlike structure that serves as a support for the anther.
 
• **Pistil**- The **pistil** is the **female reproductive organ** of a flower and consists of three parts: **the stigma, style, and ovary**. 
 
• Stigma- The uppermost component or receptive tip of carpels in a flower's **gynoecium**.
 
• **Style:** The stalk that joins the stigma and the ovary is long and slender, like a tube.
 
• **Ovary- **The ductless reproductive gland that contains **a large number of ovules** is known as the** ovary.** It is the portion of the plant where seed production occurs.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The following are the components that make up the **vegetative section of a flower**:

 
 
• **Petals-** These are the brightly coloured parts of the flower that attract bees, insects, and birds. The colour of the petals varies from plant to plant; some are bright, while others are pale. As a result, petals assist us in distinguishing one flower from another.
 
• **Sepals-** The sepal is the green part under the petals that protect the bud as it grows. Some flowers have fused petals and sepals, and some have petals and sepals that are separate.
